sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).
values [10.0, 100.0, 4.0, 8.0, 5.0, 1.5] with units [s, percent, s, percent, percent, flat]
sources_quoted.reading: 10 s carry window; 100% base AD on-hit; 4 s Expose Weakness; 8% (melee) / 5% (ranged) amp; 1.5 s internal cooldown.

sources_quoted.quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks. | Non-{{tip|basic damage}} dealt on the same target may apply stacks only once per frame.

sources_quoted.locator: Ravenous Hydra/Tiamat/Stridebreaker 'Cleave' {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}; Blade of the Ruined King 'Mist's Edge' {{rd|9%|6%}}; Titanic Hydra 'Titanic Crescent' {{rd|4%|2%}}
sources_quoted.reading: {{rd|A|B}} is unambiguously {melee = A, ranged = B} across every calibration item in the cache. Therefore Expose Weakness is 8% melee / 5% ranged, never the reverse.

sources_quoted.quote: m(R) = 100 / (100 + R)  (apply_resistance, resistance.py) ... reduce_resistance(R, r_flat, r_pct): R <- R - r_flat; R <- R*(1 - r_pct/100)  [flat first, then %] ; apply_{armor,magic}_penetration(R, f, p): R <- max(0, R*(1 - p) - f)
sources_quoted.reading: Resistance *reduction* (Carve) is a target-side debuff applied to the target's armor before any attacker-side penetration; penetration is attacker-private. A target-side debuff is therefore visible to every attacker in the roster, not only to the item holder. The same is explicitly true of Expose Weakness, which the wiki text scopes as 'increased damage from all sources' (S1).

sources_quoted.locator: Section 2.3 item 2 + Section 5 audit table row 'Terminus/BC ramps'
sources_quoted.quote: Black Cleaver average stacks (ArmorReductionEffect.average_reduction): the established model uses a fixed 0.8*max_stacks constant (with a hits/2 short-fight branch) ... the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp min(k, C) over h hits is C - C(C-1)/(2h) for h >= C; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +-20% at the extremes.
sources_quoted.reading: Provides the second candidate mechanism for an upward revision on a Black Cleaver scenario (constant 4.0 stacks = 24% -> Cesaro mean, which exceeds 24% for h > 10 hits).

independent_computation.limitation_stated_up_front: The golden scenario's input tuple (participants, levels, target resistances, fight window) lives in scripts/ and tests/, which this investigation is forbidden to read, and it is not mirrored anywhere under data/ (grep for 'cleaver_bloodsong', 'coupled_scenarios', '847.3', '892.5' over the whole export returns nothing; data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json contains 22 unrelated scenarios). The value therefore cannot be re-derived from first principles end-to-end. What CAN be derived exactly from the cached wiki text is the *transformation* between the two values, and whether that transformation is a sourced game rule.

step_1_implied_multiplier.rounding_band: both endpoints are reported to 1 dp, so the true multiplier lies in [892.45/847.35, 892.55/847.25] = [1.0532248, 1.0534671]

step_3_additive_cross_check.computation: delta / amp = amplified sub-total. 45.2 / 0.08 = 565.0 exactly; 45.2 / 0.05 = 904.0 exactly.
step_3_additive_cross_check.conclusion: The 5% (ranged) reading is impossible on its face: it would require 904.0 of damage to be amplified inside a source whose *pre-amp* total is only 847.3. The 8% (melee) reading gives an amplified sub-total of 565.0 out of 847.3, i.e. 66.68% of the source's damage sitting inside the 4-second Expose Weakness window - a physically sensible partial-window share (e.g. 4 s of amp over a 6 s window, or 2 of 3 hits). The melee value is also the correct one to read out of {{rd|8%|5%}} per the cache-wide calibration in S4.

step_4_direction_of_the_change_against_t.rule_1: S1: Expose Weakness makes the target 'take 8%/5% increased damage FROM ALL SOURCES'. It is a debuff on the target, so in a roster fight every participant's damage into that target is amplified, not just the Bloodsong holder's. A breakdown row that carried none of that amp was under-reporting a sourced mechanic.
step_4_direction_of_the_change_against_t.rule_2: S3 + S5: Carve is 6% armor REDUCTION per stack (30% at 5), i.e. a modification of the target's armor stat evaluated before any attacker-side penetration - again shared by the whole roster. Same directionality: sharing a target-side debuff can only raise other participants' totals.
step_4_direction_of_the_change_against_t.rule_3: S6: if the revision were instead the Black Cleaver stack model (fixed 0.8*C = 4.0 stacks = 24% -> exact Cesaro mean C - C(C-1)/(2h) = 5 - 10/h stacks), the change is also upward for any fight longer than ~10 hits, and moves an admitted tuning constant onto the exact mean.
step_4_direction_of_the_change_against_t.conclusion: Every mechanism that the scenario name ('cleaver' + 'bloodsong' + 'roster') and the cached wiki text can supply produces an INCREASE for a non-holder / partially-covered damage row. The old value 847.3 is the one that omits a sourced target-side effect; the new value 892.5 is the one that carries it.

step_5_falsification_attempts: Could 892.5 be an over-application (double-counted amp)? A double application would show 1.08^2 = 1.1664 or 1.08 x 1.05 = 1.134 - the observed 1.05333 is smaller than a single full application, so nothing is double-counted.

Could 892.5 wrongly use the melee 8% where the roster's Bloodsong holder is ranged (correct = 875.5, verdict both_wrong)? Not excludable from data/ alone, because the holder's melee/ranged flag is a scenario input. It is, however, the less likely branch: a 5%-amp reading of the same delta demands an amplified sub-total (904.0) larger than the whole source (847.3), so the engine that produced 892.5 is at minimum applying the amp with a self-consistent partial-window share, and Bloodsong is a melee-support staple.

Could the delta be pure Carve sharing rather than the amp? Possible, but it needs the source to be only partly physical or the target's armor to be small: sharing a 24-30% armor cut on a fully physical row against a level-18 armor value produces multipliers well above 1.05 (e.g. 100 armor, 24% cut -> 200/176 = 1.136). Either way the direction and the verdict are unchanged.
independent_computation.bottom_line: The transformation 847.3 -> 892.5 is exactly (1 + 0.08 x 2/3) to within the reported precision. 0.08 is the melee branch of Bloodsong's Expose Weakness as written in the cached wiki text, and that text scopes the amplifier to 'all sources' - a target-side debuff that a roster/coupled scenario must apply to this breakdown row. No sourced rule produces 847.3 from 892.5 in the other direction.

residual_uncertainty: Scenario inputs are unreadable under this runbook, so this is a rule-conformance verification of the delta, not an end-to-end re-derivation of 892.5.

If the roster's Bloodsong holder is a RANGED champion, the sourced amp is 5% and the correct value would be 875.5 (verdict would become both_wrong). Confirming the holder's range class is the one check that would close this receipt to certainty.
